subject: general
question:
Consider the below statements and identify the correct answer.

**Statement-I:** The metals high up in the reactivity series are not reactive.

**Statement-II:** The metals high up in the reactivity series can be obtained from their compounds by heating with carbon.

options.text: Statement-II is true, and Statement-I is false.
Statement-I is true, and Statement-II is false.

solution:
**​​​**The correct answer is __**Both statements are false**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Properties of metals

 
 
• **​​​**The metals high up in the** reactivity** **series** are very reactive.​
 
• ​​__**Reactivity series** refer to the metal series in which metals are arranged according to their reactivity from highest to lowest. It is also known as activity series which is used to predict whether a metal can displace another metal in a displacement reaction or not. This is a series in descending order of the reactivity of metals.
 
• ​​The metals at the top of the reactivity series are powerful reducing agents so they are easily oxidized. These metals corrode very easily.
 
• Metals that are placed higher on the reactivity series have the ability to displace metals that are placed lower from their salt solutions.
 
• Higher-ranking metals require greater amounts of energy for their isolation from ores and other compounds. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information __**

 
• **Metallic behaviour**

 
 
• ​The metals high up in the reactivity series can not be obtained from their compounds by heating with carbon since these metals have more affinity for oxygen than carbon
 
• ​The oxides of very reactive metals cannot be reduced with carbon cause these metals have more affinity (more attraction) for oxygen than carbon. So carbon is unable to remove oxygen from these metal oxides and hence cannot convert them into free metals. 
 
• The highly reactive metals are extracted by the electrolytic reduction of their molten chloride.​​​​​ ​During electrolysis, the electric current passes through an ionic substance in a molten or dissolved state causing the electrodes to react chemically and the materials to decompose.
